correctness.rationale: The last-received-item lemma holds for any common nonnegative monotone valuation: when assigned to currently minimum-value agent, deleting the final item later restores a value not exceeding any final opponent bundle. Empty-bundle tie priority makes the first three items enter distinct agents. If a part has >=3 goods, allocate all there, omit other parts; maximality holds because each omitted item conflicts with each occupied bundle. If every part has <=2 goods, choose a doubleton maximizing its lesser singleton value, assign its members to two agents and another part to the third; EF1 follows by deleting the more valuable singleton of third bundle. All-singleton parts require at most three singleton bundles. The full four-agent K3,3 obstruction is a previously known bound. Independently checked non-additive monotone example, not relying on prior logged enumeration. All quantifiers and empty/one-part cases addressed.
